assertion.name: Vertical transmission

assertion.name: Direct contact with vesicle fluid
assertion.description: Transmission also occurs through direct contact with fluid from vesicular lesions. Vesicle fluid contains high titers of infectious VZV. This route is particularly important in household and healthcare settings where close physical contact occurs.

assertion.name: Airborne/respiratory droplet transmission
assertion.description: VZV is transmitted primarily via the airborne route through inhalation of infectious aerosols or respiratory droplets from an infected individual. The virus is well-recognized as an airborne pathogen alongside measles and tuberculosis, requiring airborne infection isolation precautions (N95 respirators) in healthcare settings. The infectious period extends from 1-2 days before rash onset until all lesions have crusted over.

selected_evidence.snippet: Chickenpox is an extremely contagious infectious disease caused by varicella zoster virus (VZV).

assertion.name: Direct fecal-oral transmission via cysts
assertion.description: Direct person-to-person fecal-oral transmission has been proposed as an alternative to the pinworm co-transmission hypothesis. The identification of a cyst stage of D. fragilis in rodents infected with a human isolate implies a life cycle similar to most other intestinal protistan parasites, where environmentally resistant cysts are shed in feces and ingested by a new host. The cyst wall may protect the organism during gastric transit, though this stage has not yet been confirmed in human infections.
assertion.notes: As of 2024, cysts of D. fragilis have been identified only in experimentally infected mice and rats. No cyst stage has been confirmed in human stool samples. This limits the evidence for direct fecal-oral transmission in humans, though it remains a plausible mechanism given the ultrastructural characterization of a resistant cyst wall in rodent models.

selected_evidence.snippet: Dientamoeba fragilis is an inhabitant of the human bowel and is associated with gastrointestinal illness. Despite its discovery over a century ago, the details of Dientamoeba's life cycle are unclear and its mode of transmission is unknown.

assertion.name: Co-transmission via Enterobius vermicularis eggs
assertion.description: A co-transmission hypothesis proposes that D. fragilis is carried within the eggs of the pinworm Enterobius vermicularis. D. fragilis DNA has been detected inside surface-sterilized E. vermicularis eggs from co-infected patients, and the higher-than-expected coincidence of D. fragilis and pinworm infections supports this mechanism. Because trophozoites are vulnerable to gastric acid and a human cyst stage has not been demonstrated, helminth egg vectoring provides a plausible route for surviving transit through the upper GI tract.

selected_evidence.snippet: We provide evidence that trophozoites of D. fragilis are vulnerable to highly acidic conditions.

assertion.name: Inhalation of airborne arthroconidia from disturbed soil
assertion.description: Infection follows inhalation of arthroconidia released when the endemic arid soil in which Coccidioides grows as mycelium is disturbed, by wind, construction, agriculture, or earthquake. Inhaled spores convert to tissue-phase spherules in the lung. There is no person-to-person spread, so exposure is environmental and its intensity tracks soil disturbance.
assertion.notes: The environmental exposures that generate the airborne arthroconidia are curated separately in this entry's environmental block (arid soil exposure, dust storms, and occupational soil disturbance).

selected_evidence.snippet: Following inhalation of Coccidioides spores, the course may range from asymptomatic exposure with resultant immunity, to a subacute pulmonary illness, to life-threatening disseminated infection.

assertion.name: Opportunistic colonization of the external canal by environmental fungi
assertion.description: Otomycosis is not communicable. Aspergillus and Candida reach the external auditory canal from the patient's own surface flora and from the environment - these are saprophytes of soil, air and water - and cause disease only when they overgrow in a canal whose defences have failed. The route to record is therefore local colonization and overgrowth, not acquisition from a case.

assertion.name: Respiratory transmission of enterovirus D68
assertion.description: What is transmitted in AFM is the antecedent enterovirus infection, not a neurological illness. EV-D68 spreads by the respiratory route and is shed from the upper respiratory tract for a median of about 12 days from symptom onset, and household contacts of an infected child are frequently infected. assertion.name: Aspiration of colonized oropharyngeal secretions and gastric contents
assertion.description: Anaerobic pneumonia is acquired endogenously, not from another person: the inoculum is the patient's own oropharyngeal flora, carried into the lower respiratory tract when oral or upper gastrointestinal contents are inhaled past a failing airway defence. Because the anaerobes are oral commensals, the route and the reservoir are the same mouth, which is why poor oral hygiene raises the size of the inoculum rather than introducing a new organism, and why the anaerobe-dominant infections appear in patients whose swallowing or consciousness is impaired.
assertion.notes: There is no person-to-person route and no environmental or vector reservoir for this entry. The host factors that permit aspiration are modelled separately in `environmental:`; this block records only the route by which the organisms reach the lung.

selected_evidence.snippet: Aspiration pneumonia refers to the process of alveolar inflammation induced by the inhalation of oropharyngeal secretions into the lower respiratory tract.

assertion.name: Prolonged exposure in crowded, low-hygiene endemic settings
assertion.description: Klebsiella pneumoniae subsp. rhinoscleromatis is essentially restricted to humans, and rhinoscleroma behaves as a disease of prolonged exposure rather than of a single infecting event. Cases arise in crowded rural areas with poor hygiene and low socioeconomic and nutritional status, and in patients from endemic regions the probable exposure period runs to years or decades before disease.
assertion.notes: The precise portal of entry into the nasal mucosa is not established by the sources cited here, so no inhalational or direct-inoculation route is asserted. A PubMed search of "rhinoscleroma transmission" returns exactly one paper addressing the mechanism, Krasilnikov 1968 (PMID:5666684), and the fetches made for it returned no quotable text, so it is named here rather than cited as evidence. Two results of that search are false friends: PMID:390072 is a transmission electron microscopy study, and PMID:3950479 measures serum immunoglobulin in contacts rather than their infection. The 2020 prospective series notes that many of the mechanisms of infection remain unknown.

selected_evidence.snippet: Although considered a rare disease, it is endemic in low-income countries where hygienic conditions are poor.

Y. pseudotuberculosis survives and multiplies at refrigeration temperature, so vegetables and root crops held in winter stores accumulate the organism and are eaten raw; contamination of exactly these foods was documented in the vegetable stores of most Primorye FESLF foci.

selected_evidence.snippet: There was revealed high incidence of contamination with Yersinia pseudotuberculosis of vegetables, roots and pickled products (less frequently) in the vegetable store-houses of the majority of the far Eastern scarlatina-like fever foci in Primorie.

assertion.name: Aspiration of colonised oropharyngeal secretions
assertion.description: Klebsiella pneumonia is usually autoinfection. The organism already colonising the upper airway reaches the alveoli when oropharyngeal secretions are aspirated, which is why impaired swallowing and a depressed cough reflex are the proximate risks rather than contact with a case.

selected_evidence.snippet: Accumulating evidence projects a fading contribution of anaerobic bacteria in aspiration pneumonia at the expense of Gram-negative bacilli, with Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, becoming the predominant organisms recovered from respiratory specimens.

assertion.name: Breach of the gingival mucosal barrier as portal
assertion.description: The step that lets the resident flora reach deep tissue is loss of the gingival mucosal barrier, typically at an acute necrotizing gingivitis lesion. Poor oral hygiene and the preceding gingival ulceration are therefore the proximate route into the soft tissues of the face.

selected_evidence.snippet: Current studies suggest that evolution of ANG to noma requires infection by a consortium of microorganisms with Fusobacterium necrophorum and Prevotella intermedia as the suspected key players.

assertion.name: Endogenous opportunistic overgrowth of resident oral flora

Recording the route this way is the point of the record, since the disease's geography reflects poverty and not an exposure source.

assertion.name: Inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta
assertion.description: The usual route is respiratory. Virus shed in the urine, droppings and nesting material of an infected rodent is aerosolized when the material is disturbed, and people are infected by inhaling it. This is why the epidemiology tracks rodent population dynamics, and why rural occupational and recreational activity in enclosed spaces with rodent infestation is the typical exposure context.

selected_evidence.snippet: Using viral whole-genome sequencing (WGS), we identified the likely site of transmission and discovered SNV in multiple rodent species not previously known to carry the virus.

assertion.name: Person-to-person transmission of Andes virus
assertion.description: Andes virus is the exception to the rule that hantaviruses do not pass between people. In a prospective Chilean household study, sex partners of index patients were at far higher risk than other household members, and person-to-person transmission was established in several secondary cases. This route is specific to ANDV and should not be generalized to Sin Nombre virus or the other New World species.

selected_evidence.snippet: The risk of HCPS was 17.6% among sex partners of index case patients, versus 1.2% among other household contacts (P<.001).

assertion.name: Contiguous spread from an oropharyngeal focus to the internal jugular vein
assertion.description: Lemierre syndrome is not transmitted between people. Fusobacterium necrophorum is already a member of the patient's own oropharyngeal flora; the syndrome begins when a tonsillar or pharyngeal infection extends locally into the parapharyngeal space and reaches the wall of the internal jugular vein, producing septic thrombophlebitis and then metastatic emboli.
assertion.notes: The route is local extension from an endogenous focus, so there is no person-to-person transmission and no environmental or vector exposure to record. What can be acquired from another person is pharyngitis, not the syndrome.

selected_evidence.snippet: The obligate Gram-negative anaerobic bacterium Fusobacterium necrophorum (FN), part of the oropharyngeal flora, constitutes the most common causative organism of this syndrome.
